task: Correct support customer composer page capability rendering and truthful owner-denial copy

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a security-sensitive UI authorization display change, so it retains critical denial/role/tenant/Pro restrictions and negative scenarios, but can claim only source and CI evidence; it does not prove managed Supabase authorization or message delivery.

acceptanceCriteria: Support role authorization is read exclusively from hasStoreCapability instead of a misleading extra-permission gate.
Denied or inactive staff do not receive OfficeNewEmailComposer even when a valid Pro workspace exists.
The warning text identifies role status and individual owner restriction without instructing extra grant requests.
Draft revision, tenant and configured sender protections remain server-side and unchanged.
invariants: The server still performs canonical capability evaluation before rendering any composer.
Personal drafts remain restricted to the author and scoped to one instance.
Pro subscription entitlement is a separate prerequisite to the workspace.
A mailbox-less draft may be saved without pretending an email was sent.
forbiddenStates: Client-side role guesses replace database capability evaluation.
Owner-denied staff receive interactive compose controls.
The frontend reports draft or delivery success without server confirmation.
Pro-only Digital Office becomes available to an Alap member.

failureModes: A legacy 'extra' explanatory notice encourages pointless owner elevation.
A frontend boolean bypass shows unauthorized composer despite SQL deny.
An inactive role binding continues to render a previously authorized composer.
Regression snapshots fail to detect a new mismatch between page and canonical evaluator.
edgeCases: An active support agent inherited compose through the earlier SQL-only release unit.
An active support agent has an explicit matching deny and sees no composer.
A shop owner sees their own composer without a separate extra grant.
Missing role/Office database foundation renders a fail-closed notice.
An active Pro user has no Office sending mailbox but can still save their draft.

alternatives.summary: Use the canonical hasStoreCapability result and explain inherited role versus individual owner denial.
alternatives.reason: The page reflects the server permission authority and does not duplicate authorization logic.

alternatives.summary: Force the compose UI visible whenever the browser thinks the staff role is support.
alternatives.reason: A browser-side role shortcut would ignore the owner's explicit deny and could mislead end users.

alternatives.summary: Keep the separate extra grant requirement and ask owners to manually enable every employee.
alternatives.reason: This contradicts the accepted support role default and increases administrative friction for no security benefit.

specialistReviews.finding: The page may accidentally render compose controls without honoring the owner explicit deny override.
specialistReviews.resolution: Retain server hasStoreCapability as the only conditional composer gate, and check denied state in test.

specialistReviews.finding: A saved draft is not the same as a successful send and should never be falsely reported to staff.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep server revision acknowledgment and mailbox send gate, with no claim of delivered email.

specialistReviews.finding: Updating the page text alone could hide a pre-existing missing inherited SQL role grant.
specialistReviews.resolution: Make the page PR depend on the separate SQL-only role-preset source unit #1442.

specialistReviews.finding: A stack against an unmerged database change can appear correct in CI while the hosting environment remains old.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep both PRs DRAFT and require release dependency order and real Pro tenant user testing.

challenge.scenario: Authorized support agent opens a new customer email page.
challenge.finding: Historical page tells user to request extra permission.
challenge.resolution: Use inherited capability evaluation and corrected warning text.

challenge.scenario: Owner explicitly denies email compose for an active support user.
challenge.finding: A frontend role shortcut would display unauthorized controls.
challenge.resolution: Gate the entire component on server capability result.

challenge.scenario: A different user opens another employee's draft path.
challenge.finding: Unscoped UI could reveal personal draft content.
challenge.resolution: Preserve author id and instance filter in the existing page.

challenge.scenario: An employee's role binding has expired or been revoked.
challenge.finding: Cached permission assumptions could still display the editor.
challenge.resolution: Keep force-dynamic page and fresh server capability evaluation.

challenge.scenario: A Pro tenant has no approved outgoing Office mailbox.
challenge.finding: A visible send button could imply configured email delivery.
challenge.resolution: Keep active mailbox preflight and disabled send separately.

challenge.scenario: An Alap tenant attempts to open the nested Pro Office route.
challenge.finding: Role eligibility alone might be mistaken for plan entitlement.
challenge.resolution: Preserve the parent layout's strict Pro feature gate.

challenge.scenario: The permission catalog RPC fails while page data still loads.
challenge.finding: A silent allow could expose the editing interface.
challenge.resolution: Keep capability fail-closed and foundation error handling.

challenge.scenario: An audit screenshot shows old opt-in text after UI deployment.
challenge.finding: Wrong instructions may trigger unnecessary privilege escalation.
challenge.resolution: Assert the old wording is removed by regression tests.

proofPlan: Verify independent parent SQL-only unit SHA and exact child change-base relationship.
Run Plan Before Code against the admin page and unit regression file before editing either.
Prove inherited capability and explicit owner deny are unchanged server decisions.
Run exact-head CI plus later authenticated Pro owner/support/denied member journeys before release.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The customer composer page incorrectly says support must receive a separate extra email permission despite the accepted inherited role authority; this prevents proper usability and makes owner denial ambiguous.
observableOutcomes: Support staff see the composer when canonical server-side evaluateStoreCapability grants the inherited role permission.
An owner-denied support member sees an accurate restricted-state explanation rather than a request for extra permission.
No additional grant logic is created in the web page; Pro-only workspace and mail sending guards remain unchanged.
unresolvedRisks: The UI read gate cannot demonstrate real hosted Supabase draft writes without managed Auth and migration adoption.
SQL role-preset unit #1442 is an unmerged DRAFT dependency and cannot be assumed deployed.
Static render tests cannot demonstrate all browser sessions, active-role revocation or mailbox delivery.

in: Edit the existing customer new-email composer page and add targeted static regression tests.
Keep canonical hasStoreCapability decision and accurately explain explicit owner deny.
out: No SQL migration edits, no mailbox activation, no email worker or entitlement changes.
No unrelated admin redesign, Builder changes or production deploy.

requirements.requirement: The customer composer renders for server-authorized support and remains hidden for owner-denied staff.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No local permission bypass, Alap Pro-workspace access or false draft-saved state is introduced.

notes: Stacked UI-only source correction. Base is the first SQL-preset unit exact SHA, not main. The earlier mixed PR #1431 remains unverified and is not treated as a prior plan approval. The actual page edit, not the excluded active-plan metadata, is the required semantic MUST_EDIT implementation. Rebased after the first source-only unit had its known tested implementation SHA; the earlier combined #1431 remains DRAFT and unverified. Pinned to SQL parent exact metadata closure HEAD 59628c71b5084d65a0396c1d1cfa7de8fbe91b7d; no change to UI semantics.
